title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Chen
summary: Comprehensive guide to working at Redwood: culture, role ladders, promotion criteria, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding process, and key internal tools for new and existing employees.
body:
Overview

This document provides a single-source reference for new hires, managers, and people-ops partners about what it means to work at Redwood. It covers our culture and working model, the major role and career ladders used for promotions and leveling, benefits and perks summary, a high-level hiring and onboarding workflow, a practical new-hire 30/60/90 plan, and instructions for common internal tools and access patterns.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Align expectations across candidates, new hires, managers, and cross-functional partners so people succeed faster and we maintain consistent career and compensation practices.
- Scope: Applicable to all full-time employees and long-term contractors. Role ladders and promotion criteria focus on engineering and product organizations but include manager and individual contributor (IC) guidance applicable company-wide.

Working at Redwood: culture & policies
- Our values: Customer-first engineering, pragmatic excellence, operational rigor, and developer empathy.
- Working model: Distributed-first with optional office hubs. Flexible schedules with core overlap windows (10:00–15:00 local team time) for synchronous work.
- Remote + travel: Teams may require occasional travel for planning weeks, launches, or on-site customer meetings; travel guidelines are in People Ops travel policy.
- Communication norms: Use asynchronous-first communication: Confluence for docs, Slack for triage/discussion, and scheduled meetings for decisions requiring real-time input.

Roles & career ladders
- Purpose: Provide transparent leveling and promotion criteria to support development and calibration across teams.
- Ladders maintained: Engineering IC, Engineering Manager, Product, Design, SRE/Infra, and Customer Success.

Engineering IC ladder (summary)
- E1 / Junior Engineer: Learning core systems, shipping small features with guidance.
- E2 / Engineer: Owns features end-to-end, reliable execution, solid testing and debugging skills.
- E3 / Senior Engineer: Designs components, mentors others, leads medium-sized projects, proactive in incident response.
- E4 / Staff Engineer: Cross-team impact, architecture leadership, performance and reliability investments, technical coaching.
- E5 / Principal Engineer: Company-level technical strategy, long-term architecture vision, and major cross-functional initiatives.

Engineering Manager ladder (summary)
- M1 / Manager: Manages small teams (3–6), sets priorities, owns delivery and growth.
- M2 / Senior Manager: Manages managers or larger teams, sets cross-team priorities and hiring plans.
- M3 / Director: Organization-level strategy, budgeting, and partnership with product and go-to-market.

Promotion criteria (high level)
1. Demonstrated impact: measurable product or reliability outcomes tied to ownership.
2. Scope expansion: consistent success across larger cross-functional scopes or complexity.
3. Coaching and influence: documented mentorship, knowledge sharing, and peer recognition.
4. Technical or operational excellence: quality improvements, performance gains, or cost reductions.

Promotion process (numbered steps)
1. Nomination: Manager or peer nominates candidate via the promotion request form (People Ops).
2. Evidence collection: Work samples, PRs, project summaries, incident write-ups, and feedback.
3. Calibration: Cross-team calibration meeting with ladder steward and VP-level approver.
4. Decision & communication: Manager communicates result and next steps.
5. Career planning: If approved, create a development plan with timelines and measurable goals.

Benefits & perks (summary)
- Health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contributions. Domestic and international plan options available depending on location.
- Retirement: 401(k) with company matching (US) and equivalent pension/retirement options in EMEA/APAC.
- Time off: 20 paid vacation days (starting) + company holidays and 5 sick days; flexible PTO policy for senior roles may apply. Parental leave: 18 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (paid), with top-up options for eligible employees.
- Financial: Competitive base + equity grants, annual performance bonus program (where applicable).
- Learning & wellness: $2,000 annual learning stipend, $600 wellness stipend, access to technical learning paths and conference allowance.
- Perks: Home office stipend at hire, commuter benefits in hub cities, team offsite budgets, and discounted partner cloud credits.

Benefits administration & contacts
- How to enroll: New hires receive benefits enrollment email within 7 business days of start. Enrollment window details are in the People Ops portal.
- Questions & exceptions: benefits@redwood.ai (People Ops benefits team) and People Ops Slack channel (#people-ops).

Hiring & onboarding overview
- Hiring stages (candidate-facing):
  1. Recruiter screen: role fit, salary expectations, and basic availability.
  2. Technical/functional screen: phone or take-home exercise for technical roles.
  3. Onsite loop / virtual loop: 3–5 interviews covering system design, coding, product sense, and behavioral fit.
  4. Final calibration & compensation: hiring manager and recruiter finalize offer.
  5. Offer & acceptance: standard offer letter, background check, and start date scheduling.

- Internal hiring SLA targets: median time-to-hire target: 35 days; recruiter-to-offer SLA: 21 days for high-priority roles.

New hire checklist (manager + new hire responsibilities)
- Manager responsibilities (pre-start): create 30/60/90 plan, schedule onboarding meetings, request tooling access, order equipment.
- People Ops responsibilities (pre-start): send offer paperwork, benefits enrollment instructions, and IT kickoff.
- New hire responsibilities (first day): complete HR forms, set up 2FA and SSO, join core team meetings, and begin orientation slate.

30/60/90 onboarding plan template
- 0–30 days: Orientation, access verification, read team docs, ship first small task, meet one-on-one with manager and direct reports.
- 30–60 days: Take on broader feature work, pair with teammates, own a small end-to-end deliverable, and get initial feedback conversation.
- 60–90 days: Lead a feature or operational improvement, present a retrospective to the team, and agree on goals for the next 6–12 months.

Internal tools guide (quick start)
- Authentication & identity
  - Okta (SSO): Primary identity provider. All employees must enable 2FA and enroll a hardware or software token on day 1.
  - Access requests: Use the Access Request form in Confluence or the /access Slackbot for temporary access. Standard approvals come from managers and security.

- Communication & docs
  - Slack: Primary real-time communication. Join #all-company, #engineering, #product, and your team channels. Use threads for focused conversations.
  - Confluence: Canonical documentation location. All design docs, runbooks, playbooks, and onboarding materials live here. Follow the company doc template when creating pages.

- Engineering tools
  - GitHub: Repository access is granted by team. Create PRs against the main branch conventions; include testing notes and deployment instructions.
  - CI/CD: See the CI/CD runbook in eng-infra for pipeline naming, release cadence, and rollback procedures.
  - Issue tracking: Jira is our work-tracking system. Use project templates and label sprint/priority appropriately.

- Observability & runtime tools
  - Redwood Console: Internal observability console for model endpoints, latency dashboards, cost breakdowns, and rollout controls. Access is granted by product infra.
  - PagerDuty: On-call notifications and incident escalation. Engineers on-call must keep escalation policies updated and follow the oncall runbook.

- Support & operational processes
  - IT & equipment: File a ticket in the IT portal for hardware or software purchases. Home office stipend details are in the People Ops portal.
  - People Ops help: For payroll, time off, and benefits questions, reach out to People Ops via Slack or benefits@redwood.ai.

Security & compliance highlights for employees
- Data handling: Follow the data-classification matrix. Do not store customer PII on personal devices.
- Code of conduct: Professional behavior and anti-harassment policies apply to all company events, virtual or in-person.
- Training: Complete security and privacy training within the first 30 days.

Manager playbook snippets
- First week manager checklist: schedule 1:1 weekly cadence, set expectations for deliverables, review onboarding plan, and introduce to cross-functional partners.
- Performance reviews: Quarterly feedback cycles with annual calibration for compensation decisions. Use the template in People Ops for consistent write-ups.

Questions or corrections
If you find an inaccuracy or want to suggest improvements, please submit a doc update request on Confluence and notify People Ops (#people-ops) or the document owner. For urgent policy clarifications, email people-ops@redwood.ai.
